title: Framing: Toward Clarification of a Fractured Paradigm
used_for: Defines framing through selection and salience and supplies the four frame functions used to design the CASE-002 frame-intensity pilot: problem definition, causal interpretation, moral evaluation, and treatment recommendation.
quality_notes: Foundational peer-reviewed framing article. It is a theoretical synthesis rather than a validated intensity scale, so Aletheia operationalizes and pilots its elements without claiming that Entman supplied the composite score.
citation_text: Entman, R. M. (1993). Framing: Toward clarification of a fractured paradigm. Journal of Communication, 43(4), 51–58. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1460-2466.1993.tb01304.x

title: Toward a Theory of Press-State Relations in the United States
used_for: Grounds the claim that the range of news discourse can track elite and governmental debate; supports treating the press as both actor and conduit of power.
quality_notes: Foundational peer-reviewed indexing-hypothesis article; US context must not be generalized without qualification.
citation_text: Bennett, W. L. (1990). Toward a theory of press-state relations in the United States. Journal of Communication, 40(2), 103–125. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1460-2466.1990.tb02265.x

title: Cascading Activation: Contesting the White House's Frame After 9/11
used_for: Supports the broader power model in which frames move between political elites, news organizations, texts, and publics.
quality_notes: Peer-reviewed political-communication model; empirical example is US-specific.
citation_text: Entman, R. M. (2003). Cascading activation: Contesting the White House's frame after 9/11. Political Communication, 20(4), 415–432. https://doi.org/10.1080/10584600390244176

title: Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide
authors_or_organization: OECD, European Union, and European Commission Joint Research Centre
used_for: Grounds transparent construction of the Aletheia composite score, explicit weighting, aggregation rules, and planned sensitivity analysis.
quality_notes: Authoritative methodology handbook jointly produced by OECD and the European Commission JRC.
citation_text: OECD, European Union, & European Commission Joint Research Centre. (2008). Handbook on constructing composite indicators: Methodology and user guide. OECD Publishing. https://doi.org/10.1787/9789264043466-en

title: Measuring the Reliability of Qualitative Text Analysis Data
used_for: Supports use of Krippendorff's alpha to test agreement on human-coded text before relying on model coding.
quality_notes: Peer-reviewed methodological article on reliability of qualitative text interpretations.
citation_text: Krippendorff, K. (2004). Measuring the reliability of qualitative text analysis data. Quality & Quantity, 38(6), 787–800. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11135-004-8107-7

title: The Content Analysis of Media Frames: Toward Improving Reliability and Validity
used_for: Supports decomposing frames into observable elements instead of asking a model for one holistic impression, and motivates explicit reliability and validity checks in the CASE-002 frame-intensity pilot.
quality_notes: Peer-reviewed methodological review and proposed frame-element procedure. Its cluster-analysis application is not copied into the small Aletheia pilot; only the reliability principle and element-level coding logic are adopted.
citation_text: Matthes, J., & Kohring, M. (2008). The content analysis of media frames: Toward improving reliability and validity. Journal of Communication, 58(2), 258–279. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1460-2466.2008.00384.x

title: Framing Analysis: An Approach to News Discourse
authors_or_organization: Zhongdang Pan and Gerald M. Kosicki
used_for: Supplies observable textual locations for the CASE-002 frame-intensity pilot—syntactical, script, thematic, and rhetorical structures—and supports checking reinforcement across headline, lead, body, source arrangement, and rhetorical devices.
quality_notes: Foundational peer-reviewed constructivist framework with an extended empirical example. It is not a ready-made multilingual intensity scale; Aletheia uses its structural categories as evidence loci and validates them separately across Hebrew, Arabic, and English.
citation_text: Pan, Z., & Kosicki, G. M. (1993). Framing analysis: An approach to news discourse. Political Communication, 10(1), 55–75. https://doi.org/10.1080/10584609.1993.9962963

title: Framing European Politics: A Content Analysis of Press and Television News
authors_or_organization: Holli A. Semetko and Patti M. Valkenburg
used_for: Provides a deductive precedent for coding recurring generic news frames such as responsibility, conflict, human interest, morality, and consequences. It informs frame-family labels in the CASE-002 pilot but not the intensity score itself.
quality_notes: Peer-reviewed comparative content analysis of European political news. Its generic frame categories improve comparability, but its European politics setting and media formats do not establish multilingual equivalence for war coverage; categories remain descriptive and may co-occur.
citation_text: Semetko, H. A., & Valkenburg, P. M. (2000). Framing European politics: A content analysis of press and television news. Journal of Communication, 50(2), 93–109. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1460-2466.2000.tb02843.x

title: Echo chambers of a nation on the brink: narrative warfare and the construction of reality in Israel's judicial reform crisis
used_for: Provided an external academic characterization of Channel 12 as generally perceived as centrist-liberal for the documented N12 substitution decision.
quality_notes: Peer-reviewed Israel Affairs article; the characterization is contextual evidence, not a permanent objective rating.
citation_text: Katz, N. (2025). Echo chambers of a nation on the brink: Narrative warfare and the construction of reality in Israel's judicial reform crisis. Israel Affairs, 1–19. https://doi.org/10.1080/13537121.2025.2596690

authors_or_organization: Lianmin Zheng, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ying Sheng, Siyuan Zhuang, Zhanghao Wu, Yonghao Zhuang, Zi Lin, Zhuohan Li, Dacheng Li, Eric P. Xing, Hao Zhang, Joseph E. Gonzalez, and Ion Stoica

title: Israel-Iran April 2024: UK and international response
used_for: Retrospectively cross-checks the attack's scale and novelty, reported impact, international interception role, Iranian stated rationale and the bounded uncertainty surrounding the 19 April response.
quality_notes: Named institutional research briefing with transparent sourcing, published after the sampled window. It is appropriate for retrospective cross-checking but cannot be treated as information available to newsrooms during 13-20 April.
citation_text: House of Commons Library. (2024, July 25). Israel-Iran April 2024: UK and international response (Research Briefing CBP-10002). https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-10002/

title: Order of 26 January 2024: Application of the Genocide Convention in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. Israel)
used_for: Controlling primary source for the Court's provisional-stage jurisdiction, plausible-rights and urgency analysis, operative measures, binding effect and express reservation of the merits.
quality_notes: Authoritative primary judicial order. It indicates binding provisional measures but does not determine that genocide occurred, finally determine jurisdiction, or decide the merits.
citation_text: International Court of Justice. (2024, January 26). Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. Israel), Provisional Measures, Order. https://www.icj-cij.org/node/203447

title: Summary of the Order of 26 January 2024
used_for: Provides a concise contemporaneous summary of the plausible-rights analysis, real-and-imminent-risk finding, requested relief and indicated measures.
quality_notes: Official Registry publication prepared for information purposes and expressly unofficial. It is derivative of the Order and is not counted as independent corroboration.
citation_text: International Court of Justice Registry. (2024, January 26). Summary of the Order of 26 January 2024 (Summary 2024/1). https://www.icj-cij.org/node/203454

title: Application instituting proceedings and request for the indication of provisional measures
used_for: Establishes the applicant's allegations and requested provisional relief, including its request that Israel immediately suspend military operations in and against Gaza.
quality_notes: Authoritative for what South Africa pleaded and requested, but an interested-party submission; its allegations are not judicial findings.
citation_text: Republic of South Africa. (2023, December 29). Application instituting proceedings and request for the indication of provisional measures, South Africa v. Israel. https://www.icj-cij.org/node/203394

title: The Chief of General Staff: We will not stop until we capture all the terrorists involved in the October 7th Massacre and bring all the hostages home
used_for: Establishes the IDF's 17 October public acknowledgement that its troops killed Yahya Sinwar during an encounter the previous day in the Rafah area, and its claim that the troops did not initially know he was present.
quality_notes: Authoritative for the IDF's own action and public account, but written by a belligerent. It does not independently prove every operational detail, legal characterization, or strategic consequence.
citation_text: Israel Defense Forces. (2024, October 17). The Chief of General Staff: We will not stop until we capture all the terrorists involved in the October 7th Massacre and bring all the hostages home. https://www.idf.il/en/mini-sites/idf-press-releases-israel-at-war/october-24-pr/the-chief-of-general-staff-we-will-not-stop-until-we-capture-all-the-terrorists-involved-in-the-october-7th-massacre-and-bring-all-the-hostages-home/

title: On the Death of the Terrorist Yahya Sinwar
used_for: Establishes the United States government's 17 October public acceptance of Sinwar's death and its stated intention to pursue hostage release and an end to the conflict afterward.
quality_notes: Primary record of the United States government's public position. It is not an independent forensic account and does not establish that any diplomatic outcome followed from the death.
citation_text: United States Department of State. (2024, October 17). On the death of the terrorist Yahya Sinwar. https://2021-2025.state.gov/on-the-death-of-the-terrorist-yahya-sinwar/

title: Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Humanitarian Pause in Gaza to Begin Friday Morning
authors_or_organization: State of Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs
used_for: Establishes the mediator's public announcement on 23 November that the Gaza humanitarian pause would begin at 07:00 local time on 24 November and that the first civilian-hostage group was expected around 16:00 after lists had been exchanged.
quality_notes: Authoritative primary record of Qatar's announcement as a principal mediator. It establishes the announced timetable and mediation claim, not independent proof of later compliance by every party.
citation_text: State of Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs. (2023, November 23). Official spokesperson: Humanitarian pause in Gaza to begin Friday morning. https://mofa.gov.qa/%D8%AC%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%B9-%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D9%81%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%8A%D9%84/1445/05/09/%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AA%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%B3%D9%85%D9%8A-%D9%84%D9%88%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AE%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AC%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%87%D8%AF%D9%86%D8%A9-%D8%A5%D9%86%D8%B3%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%BA%D8%B2%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D8%A8%D8%AF%D8%A3-%D8%B5%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%AD-%D8%BA%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A9

title: Hostilities in the Gaza Strip and Israel — Flash Update #49
authors_or_organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, occupied Palestinian territory
used_for: Documents that the pause entered into force at 07:00 on 24 November, the first-day release of 24 hostages and 39 Palestinian detainees, and the expansion of humanitarian deliveries during the first day.
quality_notes: Contemporaneous UN situation report, strong for UN-observed aid operations and a careful public chronology. Release figures are explicitly reported figures rather than the product of an independent detainee-record audit.
citation_text: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. (2023, November 24). Hostilities in the Gaza Strip and Israel: Flash update #49. https://www.ochaopt.org/content/hostilities-gaza-strip-and-israel-flash-update-49

title: Israel and the Occupied Territories: ICRC teams begin multi-day operation to reunite hostages and detainees with their families, deliver assistance
authors_or_organization: International Committee of the Red Cross
used_for: Establishes the ICRC's own operational role beginning 24 November as a neutral intermediary facilitating transfers of hostages held in Gaza and Palestinian detainees, while also delivering additional medical assistance.
quality_notes: Authoritative for the ICRC's own role and operations. It does not make the ICRC a party to the negotiations and does not independently validate every party's account of captivity or detention.
citation_text: International Committee of the Red Cross. (2023, November 24). Israel and the occupied territories: ICRC teams begin multi-day operation to reunite hostages and detainees with their families, deliver assistance. https://www.icrc.org/en/document/israel-and-occupied-territories-operation-reunite-hostages-detainees-families-deliver-assistance

title: Statement by UN Special Coordinator Tor Wennesland on the implementation of 22 November agreement
authors_or_organization: United Nations Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process
used_for: Provides a contemporaneous cross-check on the first day of implementation: 13 Israeli hostages and additional foreign workers released from Gaza, 39 Palestinian prisoners released, relative calm and aid entry.
quality_notes: Contemporaneous UN public statement with direct institutional visibility into the humanitarian setting. It is a high-level summary rather than a full person-by-person or legal-status record.
citation_text: United Nations Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process. (2023, November 24). Statement by UN Special Coordinator Tor Wennesland on the implementation of 22 November agreement. https://www.un.org/unispal/document/statement-by-un-special-coordinator-tor-wennesland-on-the-implementation-of-22-november-agreement/

title: Statement attributable to the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General on the situation in the Middle East
used_for: Documents the UN's public assessment on 27 November that fighting had stopped for four days, Israeli and foreign hostages and Palestinian prisoners had been released, and humanitarian aid had been scaled up including to northern Gaza.
quality_notes: Authoritative for the UN's contemporaneous public assessment and its own aid activity. The phrase that the guns had fallen silent is a broad summary and should not be read as proof that no isolated violation occurred anywhere.
citation_text: United Nations Secretary-General. (2023, November 27). Statement attributable to the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General on the situation in the Middle East. https://www.ochaopt.org/content/statement-attributable-spokesperson-secretary-general-situation-middle-east

title: Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Qatar is making concerted efforts to extend humanitarian pause in Gaza during next 48 hours
authors_or_organization: State of Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs
used_for: Records Qatar's 28 November account that the initial pause was extended by two days under the prior conditions, including a minimum release of ten Israeli hostages per additional day, and summarizes first-four-day exchange totals.
quality_notes: Primary statement from the principal mediator, strong for the terms Qatar announced and the exchanges it mediated. It is not an independent legal or person-by-person audit of detention status.
citation_text: State of Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs. (2023, November 28). Official spokesperson: Qatar is making concerted efforts to extend humanitarian pause in Gaza during next 48 hours. https://mofa.gov.qa/en/qatar/latest-articles/latest-news/details/1445/05/14/official-spokesperson-for-the-ministry-of-foreign-affairs-qatar-is-making-concerted-efforts-to-extend-humanitarian-pause-in-gaza-during-next-48-hours

title: Hostilities in the Gaza Strip and Israel — Flash Update #53
authors_or_organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, occupied Palestinian territory
used_for: Documents the 48-hour extension beginning 28 November, the fifth-day release of ten Israelis, two foreign nationals and 30 Palestinian detainees, cumulative exchange figures and the broad cessation of major hostilities during the pause.
quality_notes: Contemporaneous UN situation report with strong humanitarian-operational visibility. Exchange totals are reported figures, and the report itself notes isolated exchanges of fire, so it does not support an absolute claim of zero hostilities.
citation_text: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. (2023, November 28). Hostilities in the Gaza Strip and Israel: Flash update #53. https://www.ochaopt.org/content/hostilities-gaza-strip-and-israel-flash-update-53

title: Four Hostages Rescued in the Heart of Nuseirat
used_for: Establishes the responsible forces' contemporaneous announcement that four named hostages were rescued alive on 8 June in a joint daytime operation at two locations in Nuseirat and transferred for medical examinations.
quality_notes: Authoritative for the IDF's own action and public account, but written by a belligerent and not an independent audit of casualties, legality or every tactical detail.
citation_text: Israel Defense Forces. (2024, June 8). Four hostages rescued in the heart of Nuseirat. https://www.idf.il/en/mini-sites/idf-press-releases-israel-at-war/operation-arnon-4-hostages-rescued-from-the-heart-of-gaza/four-hostages-rescued-in-the-heart-of-nuseirat/

title: Who Were the Brave Faces Behind Operation 'Arnon'?
used_for: Records the IDF's later public account of the operation's two-site chronology, the one-plus-three distribution of the rescued hostages and Commander Arnon Zamora's fatal injury.
quality_notes: Detailed but retrospective interested-party account. Appropriate for what Israel later claimed and for its own personnel loss, not independent proof of disputed tactical or legal claims.
citation_text: Israel Defense Forces. (2024, July 3). Who were the brave faces behind Operation Arnon? https://www.idf.il/en/mini-sites/idf-press-releases-israel-at-war/operation-arnon-4-hostages-rescued-from-the-heart-of-gaza/who-were-the-brave-faces-behind-operation-arnon/

title: Humanitarian Situation Update #177 — Gaza Strip
authors_or_organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, occupied Palestinian territory
used_for: Documents the four-hostage rescue, the Gaza Ministry of Health's attributed report of 274 Palestinians killed and 698 injured, and the immediate overload at Al Aqsa Hospital after the 8 June Nuseirat operation.
quality_notes: Contemporaneous UN humanitarian report. Strong for UN-observed hospital conditions and careful public chronology; casualty totals remain attributed and are not an independent person-by-person audit.
citation_text: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. (2024, June 10). Humanitarian situation update #177: Gaza Strip. https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-update-177-gaza-strip

title: Shock at impact on civilians of Israeli raid in Gaza to free hostages
authors_or_organization: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
used_for: Establishes OHCHR's 11 June preliminary public assessment of the raid's civilian impact and of hostage-taking and dense-area captivity, including its qualified statement that actions by both parties may amount to war crimes.
quality_notes: Authoritative for OHCHR's public position and its qualified legal characterization. It is not a judicial judgment or a completed incident investigation.
citation_text: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. (2024, June 11). Shock at impact on civilians of Israeli raid in Gaza to free hostages. https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-briefing-notes/2024/06/shock-impact-civilians-israeli-raid-gaza-free-hostages

title: Major Gen. Pat Ryder, Pentagon Press Secretary, Holds an Off-Camera, On-the-Record Press Briefing
used_for: Records the Pentagon's 10 June denial that the Gaza pier, its personnel or U.S. military forces were involved in the Nuseirat rescue, while preserving the spokesperson's refusal to detail possible intelligence support.
quality_notes: Authoritative for the U.S. military's own public position and disclosure boundary; not an independent reconstruction of the Israeli operation.
citation_text: United States Department of Defense. (2024, June 10). Major Gen. Pat Ryder, Pentagon press secretary, holds an off-camera, on-the-record press briefing. https://www.defense.gov/News/Transcripts/Transcript/Article/3802209/major-gen-pat-ryder-pentagon-press-secretary-holds-an-off-camera-on-the-record/
